column1: # How people actually type Telugu in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Two kinds of spelling are here, and neither is reachable from the phonetic
#  - Words the rules get wrong because Latin spelling does not carry the
#    difference: a long vowel nobody doubles ("chala" is చాలా, "naku" నాకు),
#    retroflex against dental ("ikkada" is ఇక్కడ, "kaadu" కాదు but "vaadu"
#    వాడు), ళ written as l ("vellu" వెళ్ళు, "pelli" పెళ్ళి), the geminate
#    nobody doubles ("vachanu" వచ్చాను), and long e/o where the rules guess
#    short or the other way round ("emi" ఏమి, "telugu" తెలుగు).
#  - Chat shorthand: "nv" for నువ్వు, "em" for ఏం.
# The phonetic rules already get the regular cases right (nenu నేను, manam
# మనం, eppudu ఎప్పుడు, cheppandi చెప్పండి, idhi ఇది), so those are not listed.
# A hand-written draft of the commonest few hundred chat words; it wants a
# Telugu speaker's review. A few colloquial forms (ఉన్నావా, తిన్నావా, వస్తా,
# చూసా ...) are missing from the bundled word list, which is mostly written
# Telugu; they are kept on purpose.
# Format: spelling<TAB>telugu   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
